newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Costa Rican president collapses, rushed to hospital.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rican president collapses, rushed to hospital.

text.p: Costa Rican President Jose Maria Figueres collapsed during a ceremony in Nicaragua on Monday and was rushed to a hospital, witnesses and officials said.
State-owned Radio Nicaragua said he had a heart attack, but the Costa Rican government, while saying his condition was "satisfactory," would not confirm or deny that report.
Managua's Military Hospital said he was suffering from severe abdominal pain.
News photographers said Figueres, 42, doubled over in pain while attending an outdoor tribute to Nicaraguan President Violeta Chamorro, who leaves office on January 10.

"Jose Maria Figueres felt indisposed, for which he was transferred to a medical centre," the Costa Rican government said in a statement. "President Figueres was treated in the Military Hospital, where routine examinations were carried out and showed his state of health is satisfactory."
A statement from the Military Hospital, which is operated by the Nicaraguan army, said Figueres suffered from a "digestive ailment."
"The president is stable and they are determining whether he can return to his functions," Rolando Brenes, a military officer in the hospital's public relations department, told Reuters.

Figueres and the rest of Central American leaders are in Managua paying tribute to Chamorro. They were attending a ceremony in which Chamorro was speaking to children who had filled Managua's main square, called the Plaza of the Republic.
